title: Preferring small rhythm sections, and the limits of her early records
summary: She would rather record with a rhythm section; early on she felt held back by record people who kept her in a style.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Okay. Well, we've come to the end of your recording career to date and I hope there's going to be a lot more of it. Can I just ask you just one last question before we wind up this second session of interviewing? And that is, what thoughts do you have about the ideal recording situation? Do you favor being with a large group or a small group? If you could record in ideal circumstances, what would they be?

Well, right now, I am definitely in favor of recording with rhythm section and maybe one instrument to improvise and do the fill-ins. Although in my early recordings we used arrangements, I always felt a little locked-in having to sing within a certain limited scope to make room for whatever had been written for the orchestra. In this way I have the freedom to improvise and do some of the things I want to do. Well, you can't always do that if you're singing an arrangement. In the past -- right now I can't complain about what has been done on some of the

records and albums -- well, records especially, because it was the early records where I felt a little bit more restricted because if you'll notice most of them are strictly, I'm sticking right to the melody, you know, with a minimum amount of improvisation.

I would like to have had a little bit more freedom in being able to express some of the songs that were currently popular at the time because I believe there were a lot of good songs written in the early days that I was recording that I never had a chance to record and --
Well, I think it was because they were trying to keep me more or less exclusive, I was sort of bound and tied in with the songs that were more or less in the folk idiom and --
But would you say that white singers got the best songs in those days?
No. No, not really, but I do feel that there were certain people who happened to be in certain positions that got the songs first, and of course by the time they were made available to

you, they didn't mean that much, especially if you're trying to, you know, identify yourself with a certain -- as an artist of a certain caliber. Singers with a band were just that, they were right hand to the song pluggers, I mean this is not to say that they weren't instrumental in making the record the hit that it was because you had some very outstanding vocalists at the time who are still very much in evidence and they were singers with the bands, given maybe one chorus to sing which they accompanied the arrangement. But they were, in my estimation, a little restricted because the arrangement, the band arrangement was the thing and they just didn't have the freedom.

Some of those same people now, they feel for you, now they're not bound by the arrangement and by now it's a very comfortable situation. I wouldn't want to have to do most of the things that I've recorded in those early -- I wouldn't want to have to do them over again. If I did them with the trio they would sound a little different because they would swing a little bit more, I feel. The only one that I'm compelled to do wherever I -- it's "Loch

Lomon" and of course it sounds different every time these days. I don't get a chance to do "If I Had a Ribbon Bow": which became quite one of the songs that I was requested mostly to sing because if I don't have a chance to rehearse with the group, we don't attempt to play it because it's an unusual song and you just can't take liberties with it. You have to play it as it's written. "Molly Malone," that was another. But I wouldn't record them again because I wouldn't want to "Swing" them, you know, I would want them to sound the same. So it's not necessary to do them. Now if they want to hear "If I Had a Ribbon Bow" and "Molly Malone" they have to listen to the record.

And I don't think that I -- I might have to do something under certain circumstances with a large band, you know, with everything, but I wouldn't want to. I would rather just work with a small combination and I believe at this particular point I can say that's what I want and I think that's what I'll get. I did the GI Jive show here a few --
